definitions.gloss: candied dried baby sardines eaten at New Year
definitions.explanation: Small dried sardines toasted and coated in a sweet soy glaze, served in osechi. One of the three core celebratory dishes, eaten as a wish for a good harvest.

examples.japanese: {田作|たづく}りは{甘|あま}くて{香|こう}ばしい。
おせちの{重箱|じゅうばこ}に{田作|たづく}りを{詰|つ}めた。
examples.english: I packed tazukuri into the osechi box.

examples.japanese: {田作|たづく}りは{小|ちい}さな{魚|さかな}を{肥料|ひりょう}に{使|つか}っていたことに{由来|ゆらい}し、{豊作|ほうさく}を{願|ねが}う{料理|りょうり}とされている。
examples.english: Tazukuri takes its name from the use of small fish as fertilizer, and is regarded as a dish that wishes for a good harvest.

notes:
Literally "rice-field making," because dried sardines were once spread on fields as fertilizer. Also called ごまめ in western Japan.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {田作|たづく}りを{作|つく}る: to make tazukuri
- おせちの{田作|たづく}り: the tazukuri in an osechi box
- {豊作|ほうさく}を{願|ねが}う: to wish for a good harvest

CULTURAL NOTE:
Together with {黒豆|くろまめ} and {数|かず}の{子|こ}, {田作|たづく}り makes up the {祝|いわ}い{肴|ざかな}{三種|さんしゅ} — the three dishes said to be enough, with rice cakes, to see in the New Year properly.
